chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Hamza ibn Muhammad al-Tayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
Regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'It was not for God to lead a people astray after He has guided them until He clarifies to them what they should guard against' [9:115]
He (the Imam) said: 'Until He introduces to them what pleases Him and what angers Him.'
And (the narrator) said: '(What about) Then He inspired it to understand its immorality and its piety [91:8]?'
He (the Imam) said: 'He clarified to it what to come to and what to leave.'
And (the narrator) said: '(What about) Surely We have shown him the way; he may be thankful or unthankful [76:3]?'
He (the Imam) said: 'We made him recognize it — either he takes it or leaves it.'
And concerning His words: 'And as for Thamud, We guided them but they preferred blindness over guidance' [41:17]
He (the Imam) said: 'We made them recognize it, but they preferred blindness over guidance while they were knowing.' And in a narration: 'We clarified to them.'

key_terms.بيان: Declaration/clarification — the act of God making clear what is right and wrong
key_terms.تعريف: Introduction/making known — divine act of acquainting humans with divine will
key_terms.تَقْوَى: God-consciousness/piety — inspired knowledge of what is righteous
key_terms.فُجُور: Immorality/transgression — the opposite of taqwa, inspired in the soul as knowledge
key_terms.يَتَّقُونَ: What they should guard against — the things one must avoid to remain guided
key_terms.يُضِلَّ: To lead astray — the Imam clarifies God does not lead astray those He has guided without prior declaration

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq interpret Quranic verses on divine guidance and free will in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides exegetical commentary on four Quranic verses addressing divine guidance and human free will. The Imam interprets each verse to emphasize that God fulfills His obligation by clarifying the permissible and forbidden, showing humans the path clearly — but ultimately humans bear the choice to accept or reject. This hadith responds to theological debates in early Islam about whether divine guidance (hidaya) entails deterministic predestination or leaves room for human agency. The Imam's consistent refrain 'We made them recognize it' distinguishes divine declaration (bayan) from compulsion, upholding human moral responsibility.
